points.title: 童年启蒙
points.description: 荣格出生于瑞士东北部的一个小村庄凯斯维尔，父亲是牧徒。童年时期，荣格经历了孤独和与父母关系的疏离，这促使他转向内心世界。他表现出对自然和神话的浓厚兴趣，经常独自探索周围环境。这段经历为他后来的心理学理论奠定了基础，特别是对集体无意识和原型概念的形成。荣格后来回忆说，童年时期的孤独使他学会了与自己的内心对话，这种能力成为他日后分析工作的核心。
points.descriptionEn: Born in a small Swiss village, Jung experienced a lonely childhood marked by a strained relationship with his father, a pastor. This solitude led him to turn inward, developing a deep fascination with nature and mythology. Jung often explored his surroundings alone, which later influenced his psychological theories, particularly regarding the collective unconscious and archetypes. He later recalled that childhood loneliness taught him to converse with his inner self, a skill that became central to his analytical work.

points.title: 医学教育
points.description: 荣格在巴塞尔大学医学院学习医学，期间特别关注精神病学。在导师尤利乌斯·迈耶-格鲁斯巴赫的指导下，他接触了当时新兴的精神病理学。荣格对精神病患者的梦境和幻觉产生了浓厚兴趣，这成为他后来研究无意识的起点。在此期间，他阅读了弗洛伊德的著作，并受到其理论的影响。1897年，荣格发表了他的第一篇学术论文《论精神病理学中的心理学概念》，展示了他将心理学与医学结合的独特视角。
points.descriptionEn: Jung studied medicine at the University of Basel, focusing on psychiatry under the guidance of his mentor Julius Meyer-Grünewald. He developed a keen interest in the dreams and hallucinations of psychiatric patients, which became the foundation for his later work on the unconscious. During this period, he read Freud's works and was influenced by his theories. In 1897, Jung published his first academic paper, 'On Psychological Concepts in Psychopathology,' demonstrating his unique approach to combining psychology and medicine.

points.title: 精神病学研究
points.description: 荣格在苏黎世的布尔格赫尔兹利精神病院担任助理医师，与尤金·布洛伊勒共事。在这里，他开始了对联想实验和词语联想的研究，发展出著名的'联想测试'，成为现代心理测试的先驱。1906年，荣格将他的研究成果寄给弗洛伊德，两人开始通信并建立了深厚的友谊。1907年，荣格前往维也纳与弗洛伊德会面，两人进行了长达13小时的交谈，奠定了精神分析运动的合作基础。荣格被任命为国际精神分析协会的第一任主席，成为弗洛伊德最亲密的合作者和精神分析运动的继承人。
points.descriptionEn: At the Burghölzli Psychiatric Hospital in Zurich, Jung worked with Eugen Bleuler and began his research on association experiments and word association, developing the famous 'Association Test,' a precursor to modern psychological testing. In 1906, he sent his findings to Freud, initiating a correspondence that led to a deep friendship. In 1907, Jung traveled to Vienna to meet Freud, engaging in a 13-hour conversation that laid the foundation for their collaboration in the psychoanalytic movement. Jung was appointed the first president of the International Psychoanalytic Association, becoming Freud's closest collaborator and successor.

points.title: 与弗洛伊德决裂
points.description: 荣格与弗洛伊德的关系逐渐紧张，主要源于理论分歧。荣格对弗洛伊德的泛性论和过度强调童年经验提出质疑，开始发展自己的理论体系。1912年，荣格发表《力比多的变形与象征》，标志着他与弗洛伊德公开决裂。1913年，荣格辞去国际精神分析协会主席职务，创立了自己的分析心理学。这一时期，荣格经历了严重的'灵魂黑夜'危机，深入探索自己的无意识，记录了大量梦境和幻想，这些材料后来成为《红书》的基础。苏黎世成为他发展独立理论的重要基地。
points.descriptionEn: Jung's relationship with Freud deteriorated due to theoretical differences. Jung questioned Freud's pan-sexual theory and overemphasis on childhood experiences, beginning to develop his own theoretical framework. In 1912, Jung published 'Transformations and Symbols of the Libido,' marking his public break with Freud. In 1913, he resigned as president of the International Psychoanalytic Association and founded his own analytical psychology. During this period, Jung experienced a severe 'nigredo' crisis, exploring his own unconscious extensively and recording numerous dreams and fantasies that later formed the basis of 'The Red Book.' Zurich became the crucial base for developing his independent theories.

points.title: 分析心理学发展
points.description: 荣格在苏黎世创立了分析心理学学派，建立了自己的诊所和培训中心。他发展了集体无意识、原型、人格面具、阴影等核心概念，提出了内倾-外倾人格类型理论。这一时期，荣格广泛旅行，研究不同文化中的神话、宗教和象征系统，将其融入自己的理论。1921年，他出版了《心理类型》，系统阐述了他的类型学理论。1930年代，荣格与纳粹德国保持一定距离，但也被指责未能公开反对纳粹主义。1944年，荣格在心脏病发作后，据说有濒死体验，这加深了他对生命和死亡的思考。苏黎世成为分析心理学研究和传播的中心，吸引了来自世界各地的学生和追随者。
points.descriptionEn: In Zurich, Jung founded the school of analytical psychology, establishing his own clinic and training center. He developed core concepts such as the collective unconscious, archetypes, persona, and shadow, and proposed his theory of introvert-extrovert personality types. During this period, Jung traveled extensively, studying myths, religions, and symbolic systems across cultures, integrating them into his theories. In 1921, he published 'Psychological Types,' systematically presenting his typology. In the 1930s, Jung maintained a certain distance from Nazi Germany but was criticized for not openly opposing Nazism. In 1944, Jung had a near-death experience during a heart attack, deepening his reflections on life and death. Zurich became the center for analytical psychology research and training, attracting students and followers from around the world.

points.title: 晚年与遗产
points.description: 荣格在苏黎世附近的屈斯纳赫特度过了他的晚年，继续写作和指导学生。他完成了《原型与集体无意识》等重要著作，系统总结了他一生的研究成果。1950年代，荣格的思想在西方世界产生了广泛影响，不仅在心理学领域，还延伸到文学、艺术、宗教研究等多个领域。他获得了多个荣誉学位和奖项，包括哈佛大学和牛津大学的荣誉学位。1961年6月6日，荣格在屈斯纳赫特去世，享年85岁。他的《红书》在他去世多年后才出版，进一步扩大了他的影响力。荣格去世后，他的理论和思想继续发展，形成了多个荣格心理学派，对现代心理学和人文科学产生了深远影响。
points.descriptionEn: Jung spent his final years in Kusnacht, near Zurich, continuing to write and supervise students. He completed major works like 'The Archetypes and the Collective Unconscious,' systematically summarizing his life's research. In the 1950s, Jung's ideas gained widespread influence in the Western world, extending beyond psychology to literature, art, religious studies, and other fields. He received several honorary degrees and awards, including from Harvard and Oxford Universities. Jung died in Kusnacht on June 6, 1961, at the age of 85. His 'Red Book,' published decades after his death, further expanded his influence. After his death, his theories continued to develop, forming various schools of Jungian psychology that have had a profound impact on modern psychology and humanities.

supporter.zh: 荣格被支持者誉为20世纪最具原创性和影响力的心理学家之一。他开创的分析心理学为理解人类心灵提供了全新视角，特别是集体无意识和原型理论极大地拓展了心理学的边界。荣格对东方哲学、炼金术和神话的研究，使心理学与人文科学建立了深刻联系。他的内倾-外倾人格类型理论至今仍是人格心理学的基础。荣格强调个体化过程和自我实现，对后来的人本主义心理学产生了深远影响。支持者认为，荣格的思想不仅具有学术价值，还提供了理解人类精神困境和寻求个人成长的实用工具。
supporter.en: Supporters hail Jung as one of the most original and influential psychologists of the 20th century. His analytical psychology offered a new perspective on understanding the human psyche, particularly his theories of the collective unconscious and archetypes that greatly expanded the boundaries of psychology. Jung's studies of Eastern philosophy, alchemy, and mythology established profound connections between psychology and humanities. His introvert-extrovert personality typology remains a foundation of personality psychology. Supporters argue that Jung's emphasis on individuation and self-realization profoundly influenced later humanistic psychology, and that his ideas possess both academic value and practical tools for understanding human spiritual struggles and personal growth.

critic.zh: 批评者指出荣格的理论缺乏科学实证基础，许多概念如集体无意识难以通过实验验证。他被批评为神秘主义者和玄学家，将心理学与宗教、炼金术等非科学领域混为一谈。荣格在纳粹时期的立场也备受争议，他虽未公开支持纳粹，但与纳粹官员的交往和发表的一些言论被指责为暧昧不清。此外，荣格对女性心理的观点被认为带有性别偏见，他的'阿尼玛'概念强化了刻板印象。批评者还认为荣格过于强调个体经验，忽视了社会结构和权力关系对心理的影响，使其理论在解释社会现象时显得不足。
critic.en: Critics point out that Jung's theories lack scientific empirical foundations, with concepts like the collective unconscious being difficult to verify through experiments. He is accused of being a mystic and alchemist, blending psychology with non-scientific fields like religion and alchemy. Jung's stance during the Nazi period is also controversial; while he didn't openly support the Nazis, his associations with Nazi officials and some statements have been criticized as ambiguous. Additionally, his views on female psychology are seen as gender-biased, with his concept of the anima reinforcing stereotypes. Critics also argue that Jung overemphasized individual experience while neglecting the impact of social structures and power relations on psychology, making his theories insufficient for explaining social phenomena.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，荣格被定义为一位跨越学科边界的思想家，其影响力远超心理学领域。他的理论成为理解文学、艺术、电影和流行文化的重要工具，许多作品中的角色分析都借鉴了荣格的概念。荣格的思想在20世纪后半叶经历了复兴，特别是在人本主义心理学兴起后。他的《红书》出版后，进一步巩固了他作为神秘思想家的形象。在当代，荣格心理学被广泛应用于心理治疗、组织发展和个人成长领域。历史学界对荣格的评价趋于复杂，既承认他的开创性贡献，也审视他与纳粹时期的复杂关系，体现了对历史人物的多维度理解。
objective.en: In academic and popular culture, Jung is defined as a thinker who transcended disciplinary boundaries, with influence extending far beyond psychology. His theories have become essential tools for understanding literature, art, film, and popular culture, with character analyses in many works drawing on Jungian concepts. Jung's ideas experienced a revival in the latter half of the 20th century, particularly with the rise of humanistic psychology. The publication of 'The Red Book' further solidified his image as a mystical thinker. Today, Jungian psychology is widely applied in psychotherapy, organizational development, and personal growth. Historical assessments of Jung have become more complex, acknowledging his pioneering contributions while examining his complicated relationship with the Nazi period, reflecting a multidimensional understanding of historical figures.

self.zh: 一个人毕生都在努力整合他童年时代就已形成的无意识内容。
self.en: One is never finished with one's childhood.

others.zh: 荣格是弗洛伊德最伟大的发现，也是他最大的错误。
others.en: Jung was Freud's greatest discovery and his greatest mistake.
